description: Make the deterministic plan-runner honor plan_issue so cam plan --issue N plans issue N instead of silently planning the top-of-queue issue (CAM-154).

userStories.title: Thread plan_issue into the plan-runner issue selection
userStories.description: As the operator/orchestrator, I need `cam plan --issue N` and `/cam-plan N` to actually plan issue N so that targeted planning (and the CAM-139 drainer that depends on it) does not silently plan the top-of-queue issue instead.
acceptanceCriteria: A target-aware plannable selector exists in src/issues/select.ts: given a target issue id present in the main backlog and plannable (stage:specified AND status:open AND not blocked), it returns that exact IssueEntry, not the top-of-queue winner. [oracle: bun test]

The target-aware selector returns null (never a different issue) when the target id is absent from the backlog, or present but non-plannable (stage != specified, status != open, or blocked by an unshipped dependency); it must NOT fall back to the top-of-queue issue. [oracle: bun test]

When no target id is supplied (undefined/null), selection returns the same issue the existing top-of-queue path (selectPlannableFromFile(cwd)) returns today, preserving current bare `cam plan` behavior. [oracle: bun test]

A loop-state reader for plan_issue is exported and unit-tested (mirrors makeReadLoopPhase at src/commands/sidecar.ts): it returns the plan_issue string when present in .claude/cam-loop.local.md and undefined when absent or unparseable. [oracle: bun test]

makeProductionPlanPhaseFn (src/commands/sidecar.ts) reads plan_issue fresh on each invocation and threads it into runPlanPhase's selectIssueFn; it no longer hardcodes the unconditional target-blind selector. [oracle: grep -qE 'plan_issue|planIssue|targetId' src/commands/sidecar.ts]

With plan_issue set to a valid plannable target the runner plans THAT issue; with plan_issue set to a non-plannable or nonexistent id, selectIssueFn returns null so runPlanPhase yields kind:no-plannable-issue and never spawns a planner for a different issue. [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes:
THE BUG: src/commands/sidecar.ts makeProductionPlanPhaseFn (~line 847) builds `selectIssueFn: () => selectPlannableFromFile(cwd)`, which always picks top-of-queue by rank and ignores the plan_issue written by `cam plan --issue N` (src/commands/plan.ts) or `/cam-plan N`. FIX (surgical, follow-up (a) of CAM-151): thread plan_issue -> selectIssueFn.

FILES: src/issues/select.ts (add a target-aware plannable selector, e.g. selectPlanTargetFromFile(cwd, targetId?, spawn?) or selectPlannableById(backlog, id) + a file wrapper; REUSE the stage/status/isBlocked validation already in selectPlannableIssue and mirrored in plan.ts resolveSpecificIssue/buildNotPlannableReason). src/commands/sidecar.ts (read plan_issue fresh via a new exported makeReadPlanIssue(claudeDir) mirroring makeReadLoopPhase at sidecar.ts:212, then pass the target into the selector inside makeProductionPlanPhaseFn ~line 847). Tests: test/issues/select.test.ts (three selector cases) + a reader test under test/commands/.

plan_issue is a FULL id string (e.g. "CAM-149"), parsed in src/commands/status.ts parseStateFile into out.plan_issue. Match on entry.id === plan_issue, NOT on numericSuffix.

NEVER SILENT FALLBACK: when plan_issue points to a non-plannable/nonexistent issue, return null (-> runPlanPhase no-plannable-issue clean halt), never top-of-queue. This is the core of CAM-154 (erro/escalacao, nunca fallback silencioso pra outra issue). The CLI validates at write-time, but the sidecar MUST re-validate independently (race between write and sidecar read, hand-written state files, or the /cam-plan N slash path).

TESTABILITY: makeProductionPlanPhaseFn is NOT exported (tests inject options.runPlanPhaseFn directly). Put the branch (target -> by-id / null -> top-of-queue) in an EXPORTED pure helper in select.ts and the plan_issue read in an EXPORTED makeReadPlanIssue, so the three behaviors are unit-testable without exporting the closure; the closure becomes a thin read-plus-call.

INVARIANTS: read-from-main (selectPlannableFromFile/readBacklogFromMain read the backlog from the main ref via git ls-tree + cat-file --batch, never the working tree) -- keep it; inject BacklogSpawnFn in tests. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex-group access (patterns.md). Bun runtime: prefer Bun.file/Bun.spawn; keep the existing injected spawnSync seams.

SCOPE GUARD: this is the surgical thread-plan_issue fix only. Do NOT pull in CAM-153 (generic operator-decision gate, cam resume, BLOCK->re-plan loop, plan_approval=operator, in-progress-work conflict).

POST-MERGE (operational, per CAM-151/CAM-155 notes, not a story gate): rebuild+reinstall+restart the sidecar (bash scripts/build-release.sh --install; restart cam sidecar) so the changed selection takes effect.

Read scripts/cam/patterns.md at story start (read-from-main, Review-report reader dep-injection, ensureWorkerPane self-heal) and re-check docs/adr/0006 (phase-enum loop state machine) + 0004 (plan-runner) before coding.
